about: A small reference library for the Materials module in Inner Compass Experiences (#211). Facts are limited to well-established mineralogy and botany. `associations` are symbolic meanings found in contemporary crystal, herbal or folk practice; they are not demonstrated properties, and the app says so. `history` appears only where widely documented. Each entry cites a general reference for its factual description. Personal meanings belong to the person and are stored on their own Experience, never here. Keep keys stable; add entries freely.
disclaimer: Symbolic associations come from contemporary and traditional practice. They describe what people have taken a material to mean, not proven effects.

materials.name: Amethyst
materials.description: The purple variety of quartz. Its colour comes from iron impurities combined with natural irradiation.
materials.traits: Hardness 7 (Mohs). Often found as crystal-lined geodes.
materials.history: The name comes from the Greek amethystos, “not intoxicated”, and the ancient Greeks linked the stone with sobriety.

materials.name: Citrine
materials.description: A yellow to orange variety of quartz. Much commercial citrine is heat-treated amethyst.
materials.traits: Hardness 7. Natural citrine is relatively rare.

materials.name: Rose quartz
materials.description: A pale pink variety of quartz, usually massive rather than in well-formed crystals.
materials.traits: Hardness 7. The colour can fade with long exposure to strong light.

materials.name: Clear quartz
materials.description: Colourless, transparent quartz (silicon dioxide), one of the most common minerals in Earth’s crust.
materials.traits: Hardness 7. Six-sided prismatic crystals. Piezoelectric, which is why quartz is used in watches.

materials.name: Smoky quartz
materials.description: A brown to grey variety of quartz coloured by natural irradiation of aluminium impurities.
materials.traits: Hardness 7.

materials.name: Tiger’s eye
materials.description: A chatoyant gemstone in the quartz family, usually golden to red-brown, with a silky band of light that moves as it turns.
materials.traits: Hardness about 7. Its fibrous structure creates the moving band of light (chatoyancy).

materials.name: Carnelian
materials.description: A reddish-orange variety of chalcedony (microcrystalline quartz), coloured by iron oxides.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. Translucent, often with soft banding.
materials.history: Widely used in ancient seals and signet rings because hot wax does not stick to it.

materials.name: Agate
materials.description: A banded variety of chalcedony formed in layers inside volcanic and other rock cavities.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. Each slice shows its own pattern of bands.

materials.name: Moss agate
materials.description: Chalcedony with green mineral inclusions that look like moss or branches. Not true agate, since it lacks banding.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. The inclusions are minerals such as hornblende, not plants.

materials.name: Onyx
materials.description: A banded chalcedony with parallel layers, typically black and white.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. Much black onyx sold today is dyed chalcedony.

materials.name: Jasper
materials.description: An opaque, impure variety of chalcedony, commonly red, yellow, brown or green.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. Colour comes from mineral impurities, often iron.

materials.name: Bloodstone
materials.description: A dark green chalcedony with red spots of iron oxide.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7.

materials.name: Green aventurine
materials.description: A quartz or quartzite containing small reflective mineral platelets, often green from fuchsite.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. The glitter is called aventurescence.

materials.name: Jade
materials.description: A name for two different minerals, nephrite and jadeite, both tough and prized for carving.
materials.traits: Hardness 6–7. Very tough because of interlocking crystal fibres.
materials.history: Carved and treasured in China for thousands of years, and important in Mesoamerican cultures.

materials.name: Malachite
materials.description: A green copper carbonate mineral with distinctive light and dark bands.
materials.traits: Hardness 3.5–4. Soft, so it scratches easily. Historically ground into green pigment.

materials.name: Lapis lazuli
materials.description: A deep blue metamorphic rock made mainly of lazurite, often flecked with golden pyrite.
materials.traits: Hardness 5–5.5. Ground lapis made the pigment ultramarine.
materials.history: Mined in Afghanistan for thousands of years and used in ancient Egyptian jewellery.

materials.name: Sodalite
materials.description: A royal blue mineral, often veined with white calcite.
materials.traits: Hardness 5.5–6.

materials.name: Turquoise
materials.description: An opaque blue to green copper and aluminium phosphate mineral.
materials.traits: Hardness 5–6. Porous, so its colour can change with oils and water.
materials.history: Valued for millennia, including in ancient Egypt and by many Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

materials.name: Aquamarine
materials.description: The blue to blue-green variety of the mineral beryl.
materials.traits: Hardness 7.5–8.
materials.history: The name comes from the Latin for “seawater”.

materials.name: Moonstone
materials.description: A feldspar that shows a soft, floating glow (adularescence) caused by its layered internal structure.
materials.traits: Hardness 6–6.5.

materials.name: Labradorite
materials.description: A feldspar known for labradorescence, flashes of blue, green and gold as the stone moves.
materials.traits: Hardness 6–6.5. Named after Labrador, Canada.

materials.name: Sunstone
materials.description: A feldspar with glittering inclusions (often hematite or copper) that create a sparkling effect.
materials.traits: Hardness 6–6.5.

materials.name: Obsidian
materials.description: A natural volcanic glass formed when lava cools too quickly for crystals to grow.
materials.traits: Hardness 5–5.5. Breaks with very sharp, shell-like edges, used for blades since prehistory.

materials.name: Black tourmaline
materials.description: Schorl, the most common black species of the tourmaline group, forming long striated crystals.
materials.traits: Hardness 7–7.5.

materials.name: Hematite
materials.description: An iron oxide mineral and an important iron ore. Metallic grey when polished, red when powdered.
materials.traits: Hardness 5.5–6.5. Leaves a reddish streak.

materials.name: Pyrite
materials.description: An iron sulfide mineral with a brassy metallic lustre, often in cubic crystals.
materials.traits: Hardness 6–6.5. Its resemblance to gold earned it the name fool’s gold.

materials.name: Fluorite
materials.description: A calcium fluoride mineral found in many colours, often purple, green and banded.
materials.traits: Hardness 4 (it defines 4 on the Mohs scale). Many specimens glow under ultraviolet light.

materials.name: Selenite
materials.description: A transparent crystalline form of gypsum. The silky, fibrous “satin spar” is usually what is sold as selenite.
materials.traits: Hardness 2. Very soft, and it dissolves slowly in water.

materials.name: Calcite
materials.description: A calcium carbonate mineral, the main component of limestone and marble, found in many colours.
materials.traits: Hardness 3 (it defines 3 on the Mohs scale). Clear calcite shows double refraction.

materials.name: Garnet
materials.description: A group of silicate minerals. The deep red garnets are most familiar, but they occur in many colours.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7.5. Also used as an abrasive.

materials.name: Peridot
materials.description: The gem-quality variety of the mineral olivine, yellow-green to olive.
materials.traits: Hardness 6.5–7. Also found in some meteorites.

materials.name: Opal
materials.description: A hydrated, non-crystalline form of silica. Precious opal shows a play of colour from tiny spheres that diffract light.
materials.traits: Hardness 5.5–6.5. Contains water and can crack if it dries out.

materials.name: Amber
materials.description: Fossilized tree resin, often millions of years old, sometimes holding trapped insects or plants.
materials.traits: Hardness 2–2.5. Warm to the touch and light enough to float in salt water.

materials.name: Pearl
materials.description: A gem formed inside a living mollusc from layers of nacre. Most pearls today are cultured.
materials.traits: Hardness 2.5–4.5. Organic, and sensitive to acids and perfume.

materials.name: Shungite
materials.description: A black, carbon-rich rock found mainly in Karelia, Russia.
materials.traits: Hardness about 3.5–4. Popular claims about its health effects are not supported by evidence.

materials.name: Howlite
materials.description: A white borate mineral with grey or black veining, often dyed to imitate turquoise.
materials.traits: Hardness 3.5. Porous, which is why it takes dye easily.

materials.name: Rosemary
materials.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean, with needle-like leaves.
materials.traits: Used widely in cooking. Botanists now classify it in the genus Salvia.
materials.history: Linked with remembrance since antiquity, a tradition Ophelia echoes in Hamlet: “There’s rosemary, that’s for remembrance.”

materials.name: Lavender
materials.description: A genus of fragrant flowering plants in the mint family, grown for its purple flowers and essential oil.
materials.traits: Native to the Mediterranean and nearby regions. Widely used in perfume and soap.

materials.name: Bay leaf
materials.description: The aromatic leaf of the bay laurel tree, used as a culinary herb.
materials.traits: Evergreen and native to the Mediterranean.
materials.history: Laurel wreaths crowned victors and poets in ancient Greece and Rome.

materials.name: Sage
materials.description: Garden sage (Salvia officinalis) is a culinary herb. White sage (Salvia apiana) is a different plant native to California and Baja California.
materials.traits: Both are in the mint family. White sage has been overharvested in the wild.
materials.history: White sage is sacred to many Indigenous peoples of California, and its commercial use is a concern for them.

materials.name: Rose
materials.description: A woody flowering plant of the genus Rosa, grown for its fragrant, many-petalled flowers.
materials.traits: There are hundreds of species and thousands of cultivars.

materials.name: Cinnamon
materials.description: A spice made from the inner bark of trees of the genus Cinnamomum.
materials.traits: Ceylon cinnamon and cassia are the two main types.

materials.name: Mint
materials.description: Aromatic herbs of the genus Mentha, such as peppermint and spearmint.
materials.traits: Spreads quickly by underground runners.

materials.name: Chamomile
materials.description: Daisy-like plants of the aster family, most often brewed as a herbal tea.
materials.traits: German and Roman chamomile are the two common kinds.

materials.name: Basil
materials.description: A culinary herb in the mint family, native to tropical regions from central Africa to Southeast Asia.
materials.traits: Many varieties, including sweet basil and Thai basil. Holy basil (tulsi) is a related species.

materials.name: Eucalyptus
materials.description: A large genus of trees and shrubs, mostly native to Australia, with aromatic leaves.
materials.traits: Its leaf oil is used in many household products.

materials.name: Salt
materials.description: Sodium chloride, a mineral harvested by evaporating seawater or mining rock salt (halite).
materials.traits: Essential to life and used as a preservative since ancient times.

materials.name: Beeswax candle
materials.description: A candle made from wax that honeybees produce to build their honeycomb.
materials.traits: Burns slowly and gives a faint honey scent.

materials.name: Feather
materials.description: The outer covering of birds, made of keratin.
materials.traits: In some places, possessing feathers of protected wild bird species is regulated by law.

materials.name: Seashell
materials.description: The hard protective outer layer made by a marine animal, usually a mollusc, mostly of calcium carbonate.
materials.traits: Each shell grows with its animal and records that growth in its ridges.

materials.name: Alfalfa
materials.description: A flowering plant in the legume family with small purple flowers, grown around the world as hay and forage for livestock.
materials.traits: Its sprouts are eaten in salads. One of the oldest cultivated forage crops.
materials.history: Grown since antiquity; its name reached English from Arabic by way of Spanish.

materials.name: Yarrow
materials.description: A flowering plant in the aster family with feathery leaves and flat clusters of small white or pink flowers, common in meadows across the Northern Hemisphere.
materials.traits: The species name millefolium means “thousand leaves”.
materials.history: Its genus is named for Achilles, who in Greek legend carried it into battle for his soldiers.

materials.name: Comfrey
materials.description: A perennial in the borage family with large, hairy leaves and drooping clusters of bell-shaped purple, pink or cream flowers.
materials.traits: Gardeners use its leaves for compost and liquid fertiliser. It is not considered safe to eat.
materials.history: Folk names such as “knitbone” come from its long traditional use on sprains and broken bones.

materials.name: Mugwort
materials.description: A tall aromatic plant in the aster family whose dark green leaves are silvery-white underneath.
materials.traits: Common along roadsides and waste ground in Europe, Asia and North America.
materials.history: In parts of Europe it was gathered and hung over doorways on Midsummer’s Eve.

materials.name: Calendula
materials.description: A flowering plant in the aster family with bright orange or yellow, daisy-like flowers.
materials.traits: Its petals are edible and have long been used to colour food.
materials.history: Called “pot marigold” because its petals were added to stews and broths.

materials.name: Jasmine
materials.description: Shrubs and vines in the olive family known for fragrant white or yellow flowers, many of which open in the evening.
materials.traits: Jasmine flowers scent green tea and perfumes.

materials.name: Hibiscus
materials.description: A genus of flowering plants in the mallow family with large, showy, trumpet-shaped flowers.
materials.traits: The red calyces of roselle (Hibiscus sabdariffa) are brewed into a tart tea, known as agua de jamaica or bissap.

materials.name: St John’s wort
materials.description: A flowering plant with star-shaped yellow flowers; its leaves show tiny translucent dots when held up to the light.
materials.traits: It interacts with many medications.
materials.history: Named for St John the Baptist because it blooms around his feast day, 24 June, near Midsummer.

materials.name: Thyme
materials.description: A low, woody, aromatic herb in the mint family with tiny leaves and small pink or white flowers.
materials.traits: A staple of Mediterranean cooking.
materials.history: In medieval Europe, thyme was a traditional token of courage, sometimes embroidered on gifts to knights.

materials.name: Dandelion
materials.description: A flowering plant in the aster family whose yellow flower heads turn into round, wind-borne seed heads.
materials.traits: Its leaves, flowers and roots are edible.
materials.history: Blowing on a seed head to make a wish is a widespread custom.

materials.name: Nettle
materials.description: A perennial plant covered in fine stinging hairs, common in damp, rich soil across Europe, Asia and North America.
materials.traits: Cooking removes the sting; the young leaves are eaten, and its fibres have been woven into cloth.

materials.name: Lemon balm
materials.description: A perennial herb in the mint family with lemon-scented leaves.
materials.traits: Its genus name, Melissa, is Greek for honeybee; bees visit its small white flowers.

materials.name: Juniper
materials.description: Coniferous shrubs and trees in the cypress family with needle- or scale-like leaves.
materials.traits: Its blue “berries” are really fleshy seed cones, used to flavour gin.

materials.name: Patchouli
materials.description: A bushy plant in the mint family from tropical Asia, grown for the earthy oil in its leaves.
materials.traits: The oil is a common base note in perfume.

materials.name: Star anise
materials.description: The star-shaped dried fruit of an evergreen tree native to southern China and Vietnam, usually with eight points.
materials.traits: A spice in Chinese five-spice powder. Japanese star anise looks similar but is toxic.

materials.name: Clove
materials.description: The dried flower buds of an evergreen tree native to the Maluku Islands of Indonesia.
materials.traits: A warm, strong spice; pressed into oranges to make pomanders.

materials.name: Ginger
materials.description: A flowering plant whose knobbly underground stem (rhizome) is used as a spice.
materials.traits: Eaten fresh, dried, pickled or candied.

materials.name: Orange peel
materials.description: The rind of the sweet orange, rich in fragrant oils.
materials.traits: Dried peel scents teas, baking and simmer pots.

materials.name: Sunflower
materials.description: A tall annual plant in the aster family with large flower heads of yellow petals around a dark seed-filled centre.
materials.traits: Young flower heads turn to follow the sun across the sky.

materials.name: Cedar
materials.description: Tall coniferous trees in the pine family with fragrant, durable wood.
materials.traits: Many trees called “cedar”, such as western red cedar, belong to other conifer families.

materials.name: Lemongrass
materials.description: A tall tropical grass with a strong lemon scent.
materials.traits: Used widely in Southeast Asian cooking and in teas.

materials.name: Elderflower
materials.description: The flat, creamy-white flower clusters of the elder tree.
materials.traits: Made into cordial and fritters. Other raw parts of the plant are not safe to eat.

materials.name: Vervain
materials.description: A slender perennial with small lilac flowers on long, wiry spikes.
materials.traits: Native to Europe and now widespread.
materials.history: Ancient Romans carried sprigs of sacred herbs, called verbenae, in religious rites.

materials.name: Hyssop
materials.description: A shrubby herb in the mint family with narrow leaves and spikes of blue-violet flowers.
materials.traits: The biblical “hyssop” may have been a different plant.

materials.name: Lilac
materials.description: A deciduous shrub in the olive family with fragrant clusters of purple, mauve or white flowers in spring.
materials.traits: One of the first shrubs to bloom in many gardens.

materials.name: Peony
materials.description: Perennial plants and shrubs with large, often fragrant, many-petalled flowers in late spring.
materials.traits: Plants can live and bloom for decades.
materials.history: Long treasured in China, where it is called the king of flowers.
